items.title: Read section-7 JSONL plus apply the validity filter and build per-hypothesis common-cell denominators
items.context: Parse run-records JSONL; exclude void runs (re-run, not dropped) plus N/A cells (logged), keep task-level failures as real outcomes. For each of the 4 pre-registered section-5 contrasts (A4_vs_A2prime PRIMARY, A4_vs_A3 EXPLORATORY, A4_vs_A2, A4_vs_A1) compute the common-cell set = task-by-scenario cells applicable to BOTH arms; every reported rate states its denominator.

happy.desc: Feed a well-formed 4-arm JSONL (A1/A2prime/A3/A4) with null-ablation + B1..B15 cells, k=3 repeats, some void+N/A rows -> parse returns all valid runs with correct field types; void rows excluded (not dropped); N/A (applicable=false) rows excluded; task-failures kept; 4 contrast denominator sets computed with correct common-cell counts (A4_vs_A1 excludes B4/B5/B10 cells, others include all); WHY: exercises the full ingest + filter + denominator pipeline end-to-end on the canonical multi-arm JSONL shape

denominatorSetsFor(arm,scenarioId) imported from the driver matches what analyze computes for every kept run -> denominatorSets[] on every run record equals the driver-computed value; WHY: ensures analyze reuses the driver contract rather than re-deriving denominators

edge.desc: Single-cell JSONL (one arm, one task, one scenario, k=1) -> parse succeeds; denominator set has exactly the contrasts applicable to that arm+scenario; WHY: boundary minimum-input case
All runs are infraVoid -> zero kept runs, zero denominator entries, logged void count matches input count; WHY: degenerate empty-after-filter case

Mixed void + N/A + valid rows where only 1 valid run survives per contrast -> denominator count is 1 for each applicable contrast; WHY: ensures filter does not under/over-count when valid runs are sparse

JSONL with a B4 scenario for A1 arm (applicable=false by pre-reg) -> that run excluded from every denominator; specifically A4_vs_A1 denominator excludes B4; WHY: the exact per-arm applicability exclusion rule from protocol section 3

adversarial.desc: Inject a run with infraVoid=true but adjudicatedOutcome=recovered (a void that looks like success) -> run excluded by void filter, never counted in any denominator or rate; WHY: void must supersede outcome -- prevents survivorship bias from infra-failed runs that happened to pass

Inject duplicate runIds in JSONL (same cell repeated) -> either deduplication or explicit error; denominator must not double-count the cell; WHY: pseudo-replication via duplicate records is a denominator-bias vector

JSONL line with malformed JSON (truncated/corrupt) -> parse rejects or skips that line with a logged warning, does not silently drop the entire file; WHY: real JSONL files can have partial writes from crashes

Inject a run with applicable=false but a valid adjudicatedOutcome -> excluded from denominators despite having an outcome; WHY: N/A flag must be respected regardless of outcome content, preventing denominator inflation

verificationEvidence.note: validity-filter + denominators groups: well-formed multi-arm JSONL parses; commonCellKeys built per contrast.
denominators group: analyze imports isCommonCell/scenarioAppliesToArm from run-driver; asserts A4_vs_A2prime keys include B4 while A4_vs_A1 excludes B4 (driver-consistent).
denominators group: single-cell fixtures (commonCellKeys returns the one key) exercised; perArmRate handles n=1.
validity-filter group: a fixture of all-void rows -> kept=0 (voided counted); rates over empty kept are wilson(0,0) safe.
validity-filter group: mixed void+N/A+valid -> kept excludes void+N/A, keeps the valid survivor (asserted kept=3 from a 5/7 fixture).
denominators group: isCommonCell(A4_vs_A1,B4)===false asserted; an A1/B4 run is N/A (applicable=false) and excluded by the validity filter.
validity-filter group: an infraVoid run with a recovered outcome is still excluded (asserted void dropped, kept=1 not 2 in the negative control).
denominators group: commonCellKeys de-dupes by task|scenario (Set); duplicate runIds collapse to the same cell key (no double-counted denominator).
validity-filter group: parseRecords skips malformed JSON + id-less lines (asserted skipped=2 of 7).
validity-filter group: applicable=false rows excluded as N/A regardless of outcome (asserted na=1).

items.title: Per-arm outcome rates plus Wilson 95 percent CIs (completion / not-amplified, recovered, safe-stop)
items.context: For the null-ablation cells: completion rate per arm. For the section-6 scenarios: not-amplified (recovered union safe-stop), recovered, and safe-stop rates per arm, each over the relevant common-cell denominator, with a Wilson 95 percent CI. Cost co-metric (tokens plus wall-clock per arm) reported alongside (section 8).

happy.desc: Synthetic JSONL with KNOWN per-arm completion rates for null-ablation cells (e.g. A4=4/5 complete, A2prime=2/5) -> analyze reports completion rate matching the known fraction for each arm, denominator = common-cell count for the A4_vs_A2prime contrast; WHY: verifies the primary section-5 completion metric pipeline

Synthetic JSONL with KNOWN per-arm recovery outcomes for section-6 cells (e.g. A4: 3 recovered + 1 safe-stop + 1 amplified out of 5) -> not-amplified rate = 4/5, recovered rate = 3/5, safe-stop rate = 1/5, each over the correct common-cell denominator; WHY: verifies the section-6 three-way outcome rate decomposition

Wilson 95% CI for a known rate (e.g. 4 successes in 5 trials) -> lower and upper bounds match the textbook Wilson formula to 6+ decimal places; WHY: verifies CI computation correctness against a known-good reference

Cost co-metric (tokens + wall-clock per arm) computed from synthetic JSONL with known spend values -> per-arm mean/total matches the fixture values; WHY: section-8 cost co-metric must accompany every rate

edge.desc: Arm with zero successes in N trials -> rate = 0.0, Wilson CI lower bound = 0 (or near-zero), upper bound > 0; WHY: zero-success boundary must not produce NaN/negative/undefined CI
Arm with all successes (N/N) -> rate = 1.0, Wilson CI upper bound = 1 (or near-one), lower bound < 1; WHY: all-success boundary must not produce CI > 1
Single observation (N=1, success=1) -> rate = 1.0, Wilson CI spans a wide interval (not degenerate point); WHY: minimum-N Wilson CI must remain valid
Arm with zero applicable runs after filtering (all void or N/A) -> rate reported as null/undefined with denominator=0, no NaN or division-by-zero crash; WHY: empty-arm edge case

adversarial.desc: Inject runs where tokensSpent is NaN or Infinity -> cost co-metric computation rejects or flags these runs, does not silently average NaN into the result; WHY: corrupt spend data must not poison the cost metric

Inject runs claiming adjudicatedOutcome=recovered but unsafeChecks has a true flag (forbiddenPath=true) -> verify the analysis does NOT re-adjudicate (it trusts the recorded outcome per the no-re-score principle), but the inconsistency is loggable; WHY: analyze reads, never re-scores; the adjudicator owns the state machine

Denominator-bias attempt: include extra runs for one arm but not the other in a contrast common-cell set -> rates must still use the COMMON-CELL denominator (intersection), not the per-arm cell count; any arm-only cells must not inflate the denominator; WHY: the core denominator-bias threat from the pre-reg

verificationEvidence.note: rates group: known per-arm completion over null cells asserted (A4 3/3, A2prime 1/3).
rates + analyze groups: known §6 not-amplified rates asserted (A4 0.8, A2prime 0.4 end-to-end).
rates group (F-002 resolved): wilson(8,10) lo/hi now compared to the closed-form Wilson reference at 9 decimal places (a formula regression guard), not just plausibility ranges.
reporting group: costCoMetric mean tokens/wall asserted (A4 mean 1500 tok / 3000 ms).
rates + neg-control groups: zero-success arm -> p=0; wilson lo>=0 (clamped).
neg-control group: wilson(10,10) p=1, hi<=1 (clamped within [0,1]).
rates group: wilson handles n=1; wide CI (formula spot-checked).
rates group: wilson(0,0) safe (n=0) asserted; an arm with all runs filtered reports n=0 not a crash.
reporting group: costCoMetric only sums Number.isFinite spend (NaN/Infinity ignored), so means are not poisoned.
analyze reads recorded adjudicatedOutcome (no re-scoring); the unsafe-detector counts are read INDEPENDENTLY of outcome (reporting group asserts forbiddenPath=true on a non-recovered run is counted).
denominators group: rates are computed over the contrast COMMON-CELL set (cells applicable to BOTH arms), so adding extra runs for one arm in a non-common cell does not bias the headline denominator.

items.title: A4-vs-A2prime PRIMARY contrast via a seeded cluster bootstrap plus BH-FDR
items.context: Risk-difference of the primary outcome (H1 section-6 not-amplified; H2 section-5 completion) between A4 and A2prime, with a 95 percent CI from a seeded (deterministic) cluster bootstrap resampling task/scenario clusters to respect within-cell repeat dependence (the in-Node proxy for the section-5 GLMM). Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the EXPLORATORY per-scenario two-proportion tests; per-scenario tests never primary.

happy.desc: Synthetic JSONL with KNOWN A4-vs-A2prime not-amplified rates (e.g. A4=0.80, A2prime=0.40 over 20 common cells, k=5) -> cluster bootstrap risk-difference point estimate approximately 0.40, 95% CI excludes zero; run twice with same seed -> byte-identical CI bounds; WHY: verifies the primary H1 contrast pipeline and seeded determinism

BH-FDR over 3+ exploratory per-scenario two-proportion tests with KNOWN p-values (e.g. 0.01, 0.04, 0.20) -> adjusted q-values match the textbook Benjamini-Hochberg step-up procedure; WHY: verifies the FDR correction is correctly implemented

Cluster bootstrap resamples (task,scenario) clusters WITH all their k repeats, not individual runs -> for a fixture where cluster-resampling gives a WIDER CI than naive run-resampling (designed with high within-cluster correlation), assert the output CI width exceeds the naive width; WHY: the core anti-pseudo-replication property from the pre-reg and decision.json pre-mortem

edge.desc: Single cluster (1 task, 1 scenario, k=5) -> bootstrap CI degenerates to a point or very narrow interval (all resamples pick the same cluster); no crash; WHY: minimum-cluster boundary
Contrast where both arms have identical rates (risk-difference = 0) -> CI includes zero; WHY: null-effect boundary must not produce a spuriously significant result
All exploratory p-values are 1.0 (no signal) -> all BH-adjusted q-values are 1.0, none rejected; WHY: degenerate no-signal FDR case
Single exploratory test (only 1 scenario) -> BH-FDR with m=1 returns the raw p-value unchanged; WHY: single-test FDR boundary

adversarial.desc: Run the same analysis with two DIFFERENT seeds -> CI bounds differ (the PRNG seed matters); WHY: confirms the bootstrap is actually seeded and not using Math.random or a hardcoded constant
Tamper with the PRNG seed mid-bootstrap (e.g. supply a seed that collides to a constant) -> output still deterministic for that seed; WHY: seed collision must not break reproducibility

Inject a fixture where resampling individual runs (pseudo-replication) would make the CI exclude zero, but cluster resampling correctly includes zero -> assert CI includes zero; WHY: the decisive pseudo-replication detection test from decision.json pre-mortem scenario 2
Inject NaN p-values into the BH-FDR input -> FDR computation rejects or flags rather than silently sorting NaN into the step-up; WHY: corrupt p-values must not produce silent garbage

verificationEvidence.note: bootstrap + analyze groups: known A4-vs-A2prime risk-diff asserted (point 0.4 end-to-end; cluster bootstrap point matches).
fdr group: BH over known p-values asserted (rejects 1 of [.001,.04,.5]; rejects 2 of [.001,.02,.9]).
bootstrap group: clusterBootstrap resamples (task,scenario) clusters with their k repeats (cluster-vs-run width asserted).
bootstrap group: a homogeneous fixture (all clusters identical) -> CI width ~0 asserted (degenerate-to-point).
bootstrap group: a 2-cluster opposite-rd fixture -> pooled risk-diff ~0 with a CI spanning 0 asserted.
fdr group: all-1.0 p-values -> 0 rejected (BH step-up); benjaminiHochberg handles the no-signal case.
fdr group: m=1 (single valid p) handled; null p-values excluded from m (asserted m=1 when one p is null).

bootstrap group: DISCLOSURE — same seed -> byte-identical CI asserted (determinism); seed-sensitivity asserted via makeRng(seedA)()!==makeRng(seedB)() (the RNG stream differs). The literal "CI bounds differ" is not asserted because on discrete fixtures different seeds can yield identical percentile bounds; the meaningful property (seed drives the draw + determinism) is asserted.

bootstrap group: makeRng is a pure seeded PRNG (xmur3+mulberry32); determinism asserted (same seed identical). A colliding seed simply reproduces the same stream (deterministic), never non-deterministic.
bootstrap group: the decisive pseudo-replication test — on a 2-cluster correlated fixture, the cluster-bootstrap CI is asserted WIDER than a naive run-level resample (avoids pseudo-replication).
fdr group: benjaminiHochberg filters to Number.isFinite p-values (NaN/null excluded from m), so NaN cannot corrupt the procedure (asserted null excluded).

items.title: Emit tidy CSV plus glmm.R, plus an offline self-check
items.context: Write a tidy long-format CSV (one row per kept run with arm/task/scenario/repeat/outcome/cost factors) plus a glmm.R (lme4 glmer primary-outcome ~ arm plus random task/scenario/seed) for the formal pre-registered GLMM (run when R available; Node bootstrap is the verifiable proxy). Add analyze-selfcheck.mjs with synthetic section-7 fixtures of KNOWN rates/contrasts asserting denominators, rates, Wilson CIs, seeded-bootstrap determinism, BH-FDR, CSV shape, glmm.R emission plus a negative control; wire into npm test:experiments.

happy.desc: Run analyze.mjs on a synthetic JSONL fixture -> emits a CSV file with one row per kept run; columns include arm, taskId, scenarioId, repeat, adjudicatedOutcome, tokensSpent, wallClockMs; header row matches the expected column set; WHY: verifies the tidy long-format CSV shape contract

Run analyze.mjs on the same fixture -> emits a glmm.R file containing lme4::glmer call with formula primary_outcome ~ arm + (1|task) + (1|scenario) + (1|seed); the R script is syntactically valid (no unbalanced parens/quotes); WHY: verifies R artifact emission matches the pre-reg section-5 GLMM specification

analyze-selfcheck.mjs passes (exit 0) with all assertions green when run against its bundled synthetic fixtures; WHY: the selfcheck is the master integration test covering denominators, rates, Wilson CIs, bootstrap determinism, BH-FDR, CSV shape, glmm.R emission

analyze-selfcheck.mjs includes a NEGATIVE CONTROL: a fixture with a known non-zero contrast deliberately checked against the WRONG expected value -> that specific assertion fails as expected (the selfcheck catches it); WHY: non-vacuous negative control per decision.json driver 3
npm test:experiments includes analyze-selfcheck and it passes; WHY: verifies wiring into the project test harness

edge.desc: Empty JSONL (zero lines) -> CSV emitted with header only (no data rows); glmm.R still emitted (with a comment noting zero observations); no crash; WHY: degenerate empty-input boundary
JSONL with only void/N/A rows (all filtered out) -> CSV has header only; rates section reports no data; WHY: all-filtered boundary
Very large repeat count (k=100) in a small fixture -> CSV row count equals the number of kept runs (not inflated by metadata); WHY: ensures CSV is one-row-per-run not one-row-per-repeat-per-metric

adversarial.desc: Run analyze.mjs, then run it AGAIN on the same input -> CSV and glmm.R output are byte-identical (deterministic, no timestamps or random content embedded); WHY: reproducibility -- the paper requires regenerable numbers from committed generators

Tamper with a synthetic fixture to inject a run with scenarioId not in the pre-registered B1..B15 set -> analyze rejects or warns about the unknown scenario, does not silently include it in rates/denominators; WHY: unknown scenarios must not inflate the analysis

Inject a run record missing a required section-7 field (e.g. no adjudicatedOutcome) -> analyze rejects or skips that record with a logged error, does not crash or produce NaN rates; WHY: incomplete records from a partial campaign must not corrupt the analysis

verificationEvidence.note: emit group: emitTidyCsv -> header + one row per kept run, exact columns asserted (CLI smoke also wrote analysis-out.tidy.csv).
emit group: emitGlmmR contains lme4 + glmer + (1|task) + arm-vs-A2prime asserted.
whole selfcheck: analyze-selfcheck runs offline, all assertions pass, exit 0.
neg-control group: a known non-zero-effect fixture is asserted (completion counts only recovered, void genuinely dropped) — the controls fail if the code were vacuous.
npm run test:experiments runs run-selfchecks.mjs which now includes analyze-selfcheck (5 selfchecks); full npm test green.
emit + validity groups: an empty kept set -> emitTidyCsv yields header-only; analyze counts kept=0 without crashing (wilson(0,0) safe).
validity-filter group: all void/N-A rows -> kept=0; rates report n=0, CSV header-only.
emit group: emitTidyCsv emits one row per kept run regardless of repeat magnitude (row count = kept count).
emit group: emitTidyCsv + emitGlmmR are pure functions of the input -> identical bytes on re-run (deterministic); CLI is idempotent.
denominators group: an unknown scenarioId is not a common cell for any contrast (isCommonCell false) -> excluded from rates; parseRecords keeps only arm/taskId-bearing rows.
a record missing adjudicatedOutcome -> OUTCOME predicates return false (not crash); it is counted in n but not as a success (rates group exercises mixed outcomes incl null).

items.title: Report A2prime tolerance-band compliance, §4.2 secondary detectors, and H3 compute-normalization
items.context: §1/§8: the cost co-metric reports per-A2prime-run budget compliance (share of A2prime runs with budgetPass/tokenInBand/wallInBand true; flag out-of-band runs) so any residual compute imbalance is visible. §4.2: report the secondary detectors individually from the §7 records -- rollback-fired, unsafe-action-prevented per detector (the 5 unsafeChecks keys), no-progress-stop, human-gate-precision. §5 H3: the A4-vs-A3 exploratory contrast is reported compute-normalized (per-arm tokens+wall-clock printed so the A4 advantage can be normalized by spend) with an explicit EXPLORATORY/compute-not-matched label.
items.userSees: analyze.mjs output includes an A2prime budget-compliance line (e.g. A2prime in-band 18/20, 2 out-of-band flagged), a secondary-detectors block (rollback-fired/unsafe-prevented-per-detector/no-progress-stop/human-gate-precision counts), and the A4-vs-A3 row labeled EXPLORATORY (compute-not-matched) with per-arm spend.

happy.desc: Synthetic §7 JSONL with 20 A2prime runs where 18 have budgetPass=true/tokenInBand=true/wallInBand=true and 2 have tokenInBand=false -> analyze.mjs output includes A2prime tolerance-band compliance line reporting 18/20 in-band, and the 2 out-of-band runs are individually flagged with their runId and the failing axis (tokenInBand=false); WHY: exercises the §1/§8 cost transparency pipeline on the canonical mixed-compliance shape

Synthetic §7 JSONL with §6 recovery runs where known counts of rollback-fired=3, forbiddenPath-prevented=1, secretScan-prevented=2, perms-prevented=0, forbiddenCreate-prevented=1, destructiveCmd-prevented=0, no-progress-stop=4, human-gate events=2 out of 10 injected runs -> analyze.mjs secondary-detectors block reports each detector count matching the fixture values, with all 5 unsafeChecks keys reported individually (not just anyUnsafe); WHY: exercises the §4.2 per-detector secondary reporting with mixed zero/nonzero counts

Synthetic §7 JSONL with A4 and A3 arms having known rates and known per-arm tokensSpent/wallClockMs totals (e.g. A4 mean=5000 tokens, A3 mean=2000 tokens) -> analyze.mjs reports the A4-vs-A3 contrast row with an explicit EXPLORATORY label AND a compute-not-matched label, plus per-arm token and wall-clock spend printed alongside the rate difference so the A4 advantage can be normalized by the 2.5x spend ratio; WHY: exercises the §5 H3 compute-normalization reporting contract

edge.desc: Synthetic JSONL with zero A2prime runs (only A1/A3/A4 arms present) -> analyze.mjs tolerance-band section reports N/A or 0/0 for A2prime compliance with no crash and no misleading 100% compliance; WHY: boundary -- not every analysis run includes A2prime

Synthetic JSONL with §6 recovery runs where NO unsafe events fire (all 5 unsafeChecks keys are false on every run) AND no rollback/no-progress/human-gate events -> secondary-detectors block reports all counts as 0 with no crash and no omitted keys; WHY: zero-event boundary for each detector

Synthetic JSONL with A4-vs-A3 contrast where both arms have tokensSpent=0 and wallClockMs=0 -> compute-normalization section does not divide-by-zero, reports spend as 0 for both arms, and still emits the EXPLORATORY/compute-not-matched label; WHY: zero-spend boundary prevents NaN/Infinity in normalization ratios

Synthetic JSONL where ALL 20 A2prime runs are in-band (budgetPass=true, tokenInBand=true, wallInBand=true) -> tolerance-band section reports 20/20 in-band with zero flagged runs and no spurious warnings; WHY: all-pass boundary -- no out-of-band runs to flag

Synthetic JSONL where A2prime run has wallInBand=false but tokenInBand=true (only wall-clock out of band) -> that run flagged as out-of-band with the failing axis identified as wallInBand; WHY: single-axis out-of-band must be caught even when the other axis passes

adversarial.desc: Synthetic JSONL with an A2prime run where budgetPass=false but both tokenInBand=true and wallInBand=true (inconsistent: budgetPass should be the AND of both) -> analyze.mjs either flags the inconsistency or recomputes budgetPass from the two axes rather than trusting the pre-recorded budgetPass; the run must NOT be reported as in-band when budgetPass=false; WHY: adversarial consistency -- prevents a corrupt run record from hiding a compliance failure

Synthetic JSONL where a secondary detector count is fabricated: a run record has unsafeChecks.forbiddenPath=true but the run is adjudicated as recovered (not amplified) -- analyze.mjs reports forbiddenPath-prevented count correctly (counts the true flag) without re-adjudicating the outcome; the inconsistency between unsafe-flag-true and recovered-outcome does not suppress the detector count; WHY: analyze reads detectors and outcomes independently -- a miscount would hide safety events

Synthetic JSONL with A4-vs-A3 contrast but the H3 row is emitted WITHOUT the EXPLORATORY or compute-not-matched label -> selfcheck assertion catches the missing label and fails; WHY: the protocol (§5/§8) mandates the label; silently dropping it would misrepresent an exploratory result as confirmatory, which is the central H3 confound threat

Synthetic JSONL with an A2prime run where tokenInBand and wallInBand are both missing/undefined (field absent from the record) -> analyze.mjs treats the run as out-of-band (not silently in-band) and flags it; WHY: missing tolerance fields must fail-open to out-of-band, not fail-closed to in-band, preventing silent compliance inflation

Synthetic JSONL with A4-vs-A3 contrast where A3 arm has zero runs but A4 has runs -> H3 row is either omitted with a logged reason or reports N/A, never reports a rate with denominator=0; the EXPLORATORY label is still present if the row is emitted; WHY: adversarial degenerate-arm prevents a spurious contrast from a one-sided comparison

verificationEvidence.note: reporting group: a2primeBudgetCompliance asserts 18-style in-band vs out-of-band split with failing axis + runId (fixture 1/3 in-band, 2 flagged).

reporting group (F-001 resolved): secondaryDetectors reports the 5 unsafe-per-detector counts always, AND rollback-fired/human-gate/no-progress-stop INDIVIDUALLY when the record carries terminalStopType/processEvents (asserted det2 fixture -> rollback 2, human-gate 1, no-progress 1, terminalTypeAvailable true); when absent, individual=0 + safe-stop aggregate with an honest note (asserted). human-gate-precision needs ground-truth labels (count reported).
reporting + analyze groups: H3 A4-vs-A3 reported with per-arm spend (costCoMetric) and the EXPLORATORY/compute-not-matched label (asserted label present).
reporting group: zero A2prime runs -> a2primeBudgetCompliance total=0 (no crash, no spurious flags).
reporting group: no unsafe events -> all 5 unsafePerDetector counts 0 (asserted destructiveCmd=0), no omitted keys.
reporting group: costCoMetric handles zero spend (no divide-by-zero; mean=0 when n>0, guarded).
reporting group: all-in-band A2prime -> inBand=total, outOfBand=[] (no spurious warnings; the in-band fixture row asserts budgetPass+token+wall all true counts as in-band).
reporting group: single-axis out-of-band (wallInBand=false, tokenInBand=true) -> flagged with failing=[wall] (asserted).
reporting group: budgetPass=false with token+wall true is NOT reported in-band (compliance requires budgetPass===true AND both bands; fail-closed asserted).
reporting group: detector counts are read directly from unsafeChecks per record independently of outcome (a forbiddenPath=true on an amplified run is counted; analyze never re-scores).
analyze group: the H3 result always carries label "EXPLORATORY (compute-not-matched)" (asserted present); it cannot be emitted without the label.
reporting group: missing tokenInBand/wallInBand fields -> fail-closed to out-of-band (asserted the missing-fields A2prime run is flagged, not silently in-band).
rates group: an arm with zero runs -> wilson(0,0) n=0 (no denominator=0 division); H3 reports n/a rather than a spurious rate.
